I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. At 62, I know what works here and what doesn't. The soil is good flat ground on the North China Plain. The water comes from the well — I have the pump. I know the seasons.

There is only one thing to do: winter wheat, then summer maize. I grow them every year on the same 8 mu. Everyone in the village does this. It is reliable. I know the price, I know the buyers at the county market. Corn and wheat — I can store them, sell when ready. Vegetables are too much trouble, need a truck every few days, need to be young and fast. Cotton prices have been falling for years. No. Wheat and corn.

For wheat I will rotary till in October, put down the compound fertilizer with the seed. I will irrigate four times — before sowing to settle the soil, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. Rain is never enough here. I will spray twice: once for rust and once for aphids in May. My neighbor uses 18 jin of urea per mu for top-dressing at jointing, I do the same.

For corn I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. I use hybrid seed from the village supply shop — everyone switched to hybrid years ago, the yield is much better. I don't bother tilling, just seed directly into the stubble. Summer rains help but I pump once or twice when it's dry in July. I spray once for corn borer.

I won't change anything this year. At my age, a bad experiment is worse than a safe harvest.
